newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: World wheat markets uncertain, AWB says.
newsitem.headline: World wheat markets uncertain, AWB says.

text.p: The wheat market remained uncertain on both northern and southern hemisphere 1997 crops, the Australian Wheat Board's (AWB) general manager merchandising Ron Storey said in announcing steady pool prices on Monday.

"However, this is a time of year when the market is still volatile and we recommend that growers continue to monitor it as closely as possible as the crops go through their critical development phases," he said.
During the next two weeks the market was expected to focus on the progress of the north American spring wheat plantings, which were behind normal pace because of unusually cold weather, he said.
"If delays continue, this could become an important factor in the world market and therefore the Australian market as much of our grain is sold overseas," he said.
Storey said that as the spring wheat croops were harvested in late August and September, the primary influence of the spring wheat would be on the 1997/98 pool returns, he said.
